name: Basilica of the Sacred Heart of Jesus
history: The Marist Fathers took over the parish in 1897 and bought land at Peachtree and Ivy Streets for $12,000. Atlanta architect Walter T. Downing designed the church, which was dedicated on 1 May 1898 to the Sacred Heart. It was listed on the National Register in 1976 and named a basilica in 2010.
arch: Red brick French Romanesque with twin towers and spires, one of the few buildings from around 1900 still standing in downtown Atlanta.
features: Stained glass was installed in 1902 and the interior decorated in 1907.
Its parish school was started by the Sisters of Mercy in 1880.

look.d: Among the glass skyscrapers, these brick towers have stood since 1898.
The church sits on Peachtree Street in the heart of downtown.

fun: It is one of the few turn-of-the-century buildings left standing in downtown Atlanta.
journal: Brick towers holding their ground among the skyscrapers of Peachtree Street.

quiz.q: On which famous street does it stand?
